question: Should Crabbox accept fail-closed upgrade behavior for older or invalid GitHub bridge attachments in order to enforce live-session revocation consistently?
rationale: The patch fixes a real security boundary, but it deliberately changes how restored legacy bridge sessions behave after upgrade and how GitHub grant metadata is carried through bridge state, which needs maintainer ownership rather than automated merge cleanup.

options.title: Accept fail-closed revocation
options.body: Land this direction after review, accepting that legacy or incomplete restored GitHub bridge attachments close rather than continue with stale authorization.

options.title: Add a compatibility grace path
options.body: Ask for a narrower migration mode that preserves old restored bridges until disconnect while enforcing revocation on newly created bridge sessions.

options.title: Pause for broader bridge auth design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want one unified design pass for WebVNC, Code, egress, control, and restored WebSocket authorization.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed revocation
recommendation.body: Land this direction after review, accepting that legacy or incomplete restored GitHub bridge attachments close rather than continue with stale authorization.
